text:
### Observed differences

- Activity A01 disappeared from execution: in the earlier window it ran in every one of the 200 cases, about 3.5 times per case (repeating within a case in roughly 74 in 100 cases); in the later window it appears in no case at all. [OCC001, POS001]
- A01 was a hub before: about 35 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A10, 33 to A09 and 28 to A08, while A03 passed to A01 in about 88 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A05 in about 85 in 100. In the later window no outgoing transitions from A01 are observed, and A03 and A05 instead lead to A10 (about 42% and 38%), A09 (about 39% and 41%) and A08 (about 19% and 21%). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- The relational evidence agrees: A01 previously co-occurred with A02, A04, A06, A07, A08, A09, A10, A12 and A13 in every case, and with A03, A05 and A11 in 47%, 65% and 78% of cases; in the later window it co-occurs with none of them — the first group occurs alone in every case, and A03, A05 and A11 occur alone (46%, 67%, 76% of cases) or not at all (54%, 33%, 24%). [REL001-REL012]
- The surviving cycle activities repeat more often per case: A08 rose from about 6.9 to 8.3 occurrences per case, A09, A10, A12 and A13 from about 3.5 to 4.1 each, A11 from about 3.4 to 4.2 and A05 from about 1.7 to 2.2, while participation stayed nearly flat (A05 about 65%→67%, A11 about 78%→76%, the rest in every case); A03 (about 47% of cases) and A06 (about 1.85 occurrences per case) kept their frequencies. [OCC002-OCC010]
- Distances between the remaining activities shifted accordingly: A03→A09 and A03→A10 pairs at distance 1 rose from about 3 in 100 to about 20–23 in 100 observations, A06→A09/A10 at distance 2 from about 3 to about 21–24 in 100, and the dominant distance for A03/A05→A11/A12 moved from 5 steps to 4; a few pairs became more distant instead (A11→A09/A10, A09→A03) and A08→A09/A10 became less immediate. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG014, LAG015, LAG025, LAG031, LAG057, LAG058]
- Behaviour away from A01 is stable: A12 still leads to A13 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions, A06's successor mix is essentially unchanged, and A04 and A07 keep their late positions in the case. [DIR004, DIR009, POS003, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 was removed from the process, or is at least no longer executed in any observed case. In the earlier window A01 was mandatory and hub-like, running about 3.5 times per case and mediating the handover from A03 and A05 to A08, A09 and A10; in the later window A01 never occurs, A03 and A05 route directly to A09, A10 and A08, and the remaining cycle activities (A05, A08, A09, A10, A11, A12, A13) execute more times per case, consistent with the cycle now closing without its former pass through A01. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, OCC003, OCC005-OCC010, LAG002, LAG004, LAG005]

The disappearance is shown directly in four indicator families (occurrence, position, outgoing transitions, pairwise relations), each at the maximum empirical strength of about 0.995, and activities not adjacent to A01 are stable, which argues against a window-sampling artefact. Two limitations remain: zero participation only shows A01 was not observed, so a still-existing A01 that was skipped in all 200 later cases (or a relabelling) cannot be excluded; and the higher repetition counts for A08–A13 could be an independent change in repetition rather than a consequence of the rerouting. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL001, DIR004, DIR009, OCC005-OCC010]

Other differences: several activities sit slightly earlier within the case (A06, A09, A12 and A13 mean positions lower by about 0.01–0.03 of the case length), A13 routes to A05 somewhat more often (about 45%→52%) and to A06 somewhat less (about 50%→44%), and A08's self-distances shrank slightly. [POS005, POS008, POS011, POS012, DIR010, LAG024]
